title: Classifying an organic reaction
caption: Ask what happens to the starting molecule. Two molecules joining into one is addition; a group swapped for another is substitution; a small molecule lost to form a double bond is elimination. Oxidation, reduction, condensation and hydrolysis are named by what is gained or lost.
alt: A decision tree: does the number of molecules fall? If yes, addition. If no, is one group replaced by another? If yes, substitution; if no, is a small molecule removed to leave a multiple bond? If yes, elimination; otherwise a rearrangement.
description: First question: do two reactant molecules become one product? Yes means addition, as in ethene + HBr.
Otherwise: is one atom or group replaced by another? Yes means substitution, as in bromoethane + OH⁻.
Otherwise: is a small molecule such as H₂O or HBr removed, leaving a double bond? Yes means elimination; if not, the atoms have rearranged.

q1.q: Do two molecules join to make one product?

q2.q: Is one atom or group replaced by another?

q3.q: Is a small molecule lost, leaving a C=C?
